module.title: Safety and Laboratory Tools
module.description: A required MB 304L pre-laboratory orientation to safety, PPE, tool familiarization, handling, and waste preparation before guided anatomy activities.

statusNotice: Awaiting MB 304L faculty validation. General guidance does not replace the institution-approved laboratory SOP or instructor direction.

steps.title: Begin with risk awareness
steps.caption: Review the planned activity, known hazards, emergency directions, and the local laboratory SOP before handling a specimen or tool.

steps.title: Prepare personal protection
steps.caption: Use the protective equipment selected by the instructor for the specimen, procedure, and local risk assessment.

steps.title: Prepare the work area
steps.caption: Stabilize the tray, keep absorbent material available, and position disposal containers before work begins.

steps.title: Recognize cutting hazards
steps.caption: Cutting tools remain under instructor control. Use the least hazardous suitable tool and direct cutting motion away from hands and nearby people.

steps.title: Handle and position structures
steps.caption: Use forceps, probes, and pins for observation and positioning while minimizing tissue damage and puncture risk.

steps.title: Observe and measure
steps.caption: Keep the specimen contained and use the approved measurement method without contaminating shared surfaces.

steps.title: Separate cleanup and waste
steps.caption: Place sharps and biological material only in their designated containers, clean the work surface using the local procedure, and remove PPE as instructed.

steps.title: Complete the formative tool check
steps.caption: Choose the safest suitable tool or preparation for each scenario. The score supports practice and does not determine completion.

tools.name: Dissecting tray
tools.purpose: Provides a stable, contained work surface for the specimen.
tools.handling: Place it on a level surface and keep the working area within the tray.
tools.applicableStep: Workspace preparation and the supervised dissection sequence.
tools.safety: Keep the tray stable, organized, and clear of unused sharps.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Scalpel and disposable blade
tools.purpose: Makes a controlled incision when a scalpel is required by the approved procedure.
tools.handling: The instructor controls blade fitting, use, transfer, and removal; hold only by the handle and keep the cutting edge directed away from the body.
tools.applicableStep: Instructor-supervised incision or tissue separation specified by the local SOP.
tools.safety: Treat every blade as a sharp. Never leave it loose or place it in biological-waste containers.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Dissecting scissors
tools.purpose: Opens tissue along a controlled path when scissors are safer or more appropriate than a blade.
tools.handling: Keep the lower blade shallow and lift tissue away from underlying organs as directed by the instructor.
tools.applicableStep: Opening the body wall under faculty supervision.
tools.safety: Keep fingers outside the cutting path and close the scissors when carrying or setting them down.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Forceps
tools.purpose: Grasps or lifts small structures without direct hand contact.
tools.handling: Use light pressure and hold the structure only as firmly as observation requires.
tools.applicableStep: Lifting tissue, positioning structures, and handling small items.
tools.safety: Do not use forceps as a cutting tool; keep pointed tips directed toward the work area.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Blunt probe
tools.purpose: Separates or traces structures with reduced puncture risk.
tools.handling: Use the rounded end with gentle pressure to trace spaces and connections.
tools.applicableStep: Exploration of gills, organs, and body-system pathways.
tools.safety: Use the blunt probe before a pointed instrument when it can achieve the learning task.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Pointed probe
tools.purpose: Indicates or separates a small structure when a blunt probe is insufficient.
tools.handling: Use only under instructor direction and apply minimal pressure at the selected point.
tools.applicableStep: Detailed identification or positioning specified by the instructor.
tools.safety: Treat the pointed end as a sharp and never direct it toward yourself or another person.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Dissecting pins
tools.purpose: Secures the specimen or reflected tissue to the tray.
tools.handling: Insert and remove pins one at a time using the approved angle and placement.
tools.applicableStep: Specimen positioning and controlled exposure of structures.
tools.safety: Account for every pin and dispose of damaged or contaminated pins according to the local sharps procedure.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Ruler or measuring board
tools.purpose: Records length or position using a consistent measurement reference.
tools.handling: Place the specimen and scale on the approved surface without transferring contamination to clean equipment.
tools.safety: Clean or isolate reusable measurement equipment according to the local SOP.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Specimen container
tools.purpose: Holds or transports the specimen in a controlled, labeled container.
tools.handling: Keep the container closed when it is not being accessed and follow the instructor's labeling and transfer directions.
tools.applicableStep: Specimen receipt, orientation, storage, and return or disposal.
tools.safety: Do not use an unlabeled, leaking, damaged, or unauthorized container.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Laboratory coat or apron
tools.purpose: Protects clothing and skin from incidental contact or splashes identified by the risk assessment.
tools.handling: Fasten it before work and remove it using the local procedure before leaving the designated area.
tools.applicableStep: Preparation, supervised specimen work, and cleanup.
tools.safety: Use the garment type and replacement schedule selected by the instructor and local SOP.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Nitrile gloves
tools.purpose: Provides a disposable hand barrier when required by the risk assessment.
tools.handling: Inspect before use, change when damaged or contaminated, and remove without touching the outer surface with bare skin.
tools.applicableStep: Specimen handling and cleanup when directed.
tools.safety: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene and must not be used to touch clean personal items.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Safety goggles
tools.purpose: Protects the eyes when the risk assessment identifies splash or particle hazards.
tools.handling: Adjust for a secure fit and keep the lenses clean and unobstructed.
tools.applicableStep: Preparation and procedures with a potential eye hazard.
tools.safety: Use the eye protection type required by the instructor; ordinary eyewear may not provide equivalent protection.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Absorbent material
tools.purpose: Contains small amounts of liquid and supports the approved cleanup procedure.
tools.handling: Position it where directed and replace it when saturated or contaminated.
tools.applicableStep: Workspace preparation, spill response, and cleanup.
tools.safety: Do not handle a spill without the training, PPE, and disinfectant specified by the local procedure.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Biological-waste container
tools.purpose: Separates biological material from ordinary waste for approved treatment or disposal.
tools.handling: Place only authorized biological waste inside and keep the container identified and closed as required.
tools.safety: Follow institutional and local requirements for segregation, decontamination, storage, and disposal.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.

tools.name: Sharps container
tools.purpose: Receives used or contaminated sharp items in a puncture-resistant container.
tools.handling: Keep it upright, accessible, and close to the point of use; place sharps inside promptly without reaching into the opening.
tools.applicableStep: Preparation, tool exchange, and immediate post-use disposal.
tools.safety: Do not overfill, force items through the opening, or place loose sharps in ordinary or biological waste.
tools.licence: Project-original educational text; source references are linked in this manifest.
